purpose: Widely-used client-side CSS/JavaScript framework for building responsive web UI components.
description: Bootstrap versions before 4.3.1 are affected by a documented cross-site scripting issue (CVE-2019-8331) in the tooltip and popover components, where the 'title' or 'data-content' options accept HTML and don't sanitize it before rendering when a template/config allows HTML content.
common_risks: XSS via tooltip/popover HTML content options
misconfigurations: tooltip/popover initialized with `html: true` and a user-controlled title/content value
attack_patterns: Inject script via a tooltip or popover whose content is built from unsanitized user input
real_world_incidents: CVE-2019-8331 was disclosed and fixed in Bootstrap 4.3.1; outdated bundled copies of Bootstrap remain a routine finding in dependency and JS-library version scans.
recommended_actions: Upgrade to Bootstrap 4.3.1 or later (or the current 5.x line, which addressed this class of issue in its rewrite).
Avoid enabling `html: true` on tooltips/popovers whose content includes any user-controlled data; sanitize first if HTML content is genuinely required.

audience_guidance.student: Bootstrap is a popular toolkit for styling web pages and building UI components like tooltips and popups. An older version had a bug where those popups could be tricked into running attacker-supplied script if their content wasn't handled carefully.
audience_guidance.developer: Upgrade to Bootstrap 4.3.1+, and avoid passing unsanitized user input into tooltip/popover content when `html: true` is set.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Fingerprint the Bootstrap version from the bundled CSS/JS file, then check for tooltips/popovers whose content is built from user input.
audience_guidance.pentester: Confirm the Bootstrap version and test any tooltip/popover component that renders user-influenced content for injected markup.
audience_guidance.security_team: Include client-side framework versions like Bootstrap in routine dependency audits — an outdated bundled copy is easy to overlook since it isn't managed the same way as server-side packages.
